Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a type of good or material managed within the inventory and production system, such as raw cashews, roasted cashews, or packaging materials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

name.description: The common name of the product (e.g., 'Raw Cashews', 'Roasted & Salted Cashews').

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

unitOfMeasure.description: The standard unit of measure for this product (e.g., 'kg', 'bag', 'unit').

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit, a unique identifier for the product often used for inventory tracking.

InventoryTransaction.title: InventoryTransaction
InventoryTransaction.description: Records all movements of products, including goods received, dispatched, or inventory adjustments, maintaining an audit trail.

id.description: Unique identifier for the InventoryTransaction entity.

productId.description: Reference to the Product involved in this transaction. (Relationship: Product 1:N InventoryTransaction)

quantity.description: The quantity of the product involved in the transaction.

transactionDateTime.description: The date and time when the transaction occurred.

locationOrParty.description: Describes the origin or destination of the goods (e.g., 'Supplier A', 'Warehouse B', 'Customer X').

notes.description: Additional notes or comments about the transaction.

correctionForTransactionId.description: Reference to the original InventoryTransaction that this entry corrects. Used for audit trails and error correction. (Relationship: InventoryTransaction 1:N InventoryTransaction (self-referencing))

ProductionStage.title: ProductionStage
ProductionStage.description: Defines a distinct step or phase in the production process, such as 'Roasting' or 'Shelling'.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProductionStage entity.

name.description: The name of the production stage (e.g., 'Shelling', 'Roasting', 'Packaging').

description.description: A detailed description of what happens in this production stage.

ProductionLog.title: ProductionLog
ProductionLog.description: Records specific instances of a production stage being carried out, including inputs, outputs, and timings.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProductionLog entity.

productionStageId.description: Reference to the ProductionStage that was performed. (Relationship: ProductionStage 1:N ProductionLog)

productInputIds.description: References to Products consumed or used as inputs in this production log entry. (Relationship: Product N:N ProductionLog)

productOutputIds.description: References to Products generated or produced as outputs in this production log entry. (Relationship: Product N:N ProductionLog)

quantityProcessed.description: The primary quantity of material processed or units produced during this stage.

startDateTime.description: The date and time when the production stage started.

endDateTime.description: The date and time when the production stage ended.

notes.description: Additional notes or observations about this production run.

correctionForProductionLogId.description: Reference to the original ProductionLog entry that this one corrects. Used for auditing purposes. (Relationship: ProductionLog 1:N ProductionLog (self-referencing))

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores user-specific data and preferences for the application, linked to an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, internal to the Nutshell Insights system.

externalAuthIdentifier.description: The unique identifier for the user as provided by the external authentication system.

email.description: The user's email address, primarily used for sending notifications.

notificationPreferenceIds.description: References to NotificationPreference entities that this user has opted into or configured. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N NotificationPreference)

NotificationPreference.title: NotificationPreference
NotificationPreference.description: Defines a specific type of notification that users can subscribe to or configure.

id.description: Unique identifier for the NotificationPreference entity.

name.description: The name of the notification preference (e.g., 'Daily AI Summary', 'Low Stock Alert').

description.description: A description of what this notification entails.

defaultEnabled.description: Indicates whether this notification preference is enabled by default for new users.

AISummary.title: AISummary
AISummary.description: Stores automatically generated AI summaries of inventory and production activities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AISummary entity.

summaryDate.description: The date that the summary pertains to or covers.

title.description: The title of the AI-generated summary.

content.description: The full text content of the AI-generated summary.

generatedDateTime.description: The date and time when the summary was generated.

summaryType.description: The category or type of summary (e.g., 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Inventory Highlights', 'Production Insights').

ReportConfiguration.title: ReportConfiguration
ReportConfiguration.description: Allows users to save their customized report settings, including filters and date ranges, for future use.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ReportConfiguration entity.

userProfileId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created or owns this report configuration. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ReportConfiguration)

name.description: A user-defined name for the saved report configuration (e.g., 'My Weekly Production Overview').

reportType.description: The type of report this configuration applies to (e.g., 'Inventory Summary', 'Production Log', 'Item-Wise Totals').

startDate.description: The starting date for the report's data range, if applicable.

endDate.description: The ending date for the report's data range, if applicable.

filterParameters.description: A JSON string or object containing specific filter parameters for the report (e.g., product IDs, stage IDs, locations).

creationDateTime.description: The date and time when this report configuration was created.

lastModifiedDateTime.description: The date and time when this report configuration was last modified.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and clear Access Modeling to ensure security, scalability, and debuggability. 

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
For user-specific data, such as saved report configurations, we utilize a hierarchical path: `/users/{userId}/reportConfigurations/{reportConfigurationId}`. A crucial aspect here is the denormalization of authorization context. Each `ReportConfiguration` document *must* include a `userProfileId` field whose value matches the `userId` in its parent path. This allows Firebase Security Rules to directly compare `request.auth.uid` against the path's `userId` and/or the `resource.data.userProfileId` within the document itself. This eliminates the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to parent documents for authorization, thereby supporting atomic operations (transactions/batches) and simplifying rule debugging significantly.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters) through Structural Segregation:**

1.  **User-Specific Data:** Private user data, like `UserProfile` and `ReportConfiguration`, is strictly segregated using path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}` and `/users/{userId}/reportConfigurations`). This ensures that `list` operations for these collections are inherently secure: a user can only list documents within their own designated subcollection (`/users/$(request.auth.uid)/reportConfigurations`), preventing unauthorized access to other users' data. This aligns perfectly with the Query as a Security Principle (QAP) by guaranteeing that any query result is fully authorized.
2.  **Global/Organization-Wide Data:** Core operational and reference data entities such as `Product`, `InventoryTransaction`, `ProductionStage`, `ProductionLog`, `AISummary`, and `NotificationPreference` are placed in top-level collections (e.g., `/products`, `/inventoryTransactions`). This segregation ensures all documents within these collections share the same security posture – typically, accessible by all authenticated users within the organization, possibly with role-based write permissions. For these collections, `list` operations are secure because any authenticated user granted read access to the collection can retrieve all documents, effectively satisfying the QAP principle without needing complex client-side filtering or server-side rule lookups.
3.  **Role-Based Access Control (DBAC):** Authorization for specific roles (e.g., administrators, staff) is managed through existence checks in dedicated top-level collections, such as `/roles_admins/{userId}`. The mere *existence* of a document at `roles_admins/$(request.auth.uid)` grants administrative privileges. This approach avoids custom claims, is highly debuggable, and provides clear, explicit authorization without relying on hierarchical data lookups.

**Error Correction:** The `correctionForTransactionId` and `correctionForProductionLogId` fields within `InventoryTransaction` and `ProductionLog` entities provide an explicit, auditable mechanism for error correction directly within the document schema, maintaining data integrity without affecting the overall collection structure for authorization purposes.
